definition_quote.value: Practice of medicine means: (A) Holding out oneself to the public within this state as being able to diagnose, treat, prescribe for, palliate, or prevent any human disease, ailment, injury, deformity, or physical or mental condition, whether by the use of drugs, surgery, manipulation, electricity, or any physical, mechanical, or other means whatsoever; (B) Suggesting, recommending, prescribing, or administering any form of treatment, operation, or healing for the intended palliation, relief, or cure of any physical or mental disease, ailment, injury, condition, or defect of any person with the intention of receiving, either directly or indirectly, any fee, gift, or compensation whatsoever; (C) Maintaining an office or other place to meet persons for the purpose of examining or treating persons afflicted with disease, injury, or defect of body or mind; (D) Using the title "M.D.", "M.B.", "D.O.", "physician", "surgeon", or any other word or abbreviation to indicate or induce others to believe that one is engaged in the diagnosis or treatment of persons afflicted with disease, injury, or defect of body or mind; (E) Performing any kind of surgical operation upon a human being; or (F) Delegating certain medical practices to other personnel under rules adopted by the board.
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of medicine" means: (A) Holding out oneself to the public within this state as being able to diagnose, treat, prescribe for, palliate, or prevent any human disease, ailment, injury, deformity, or physical or mental condition, whether by the use of drugs, surgery, manipulation, electricity, or any physical, mechanical, or other means whatsoever

methods_authorized.quote: diagnose, treat, prescribe for, palliate, or prevent any human disease, ailment, injury, deformity, or physical or mental condition, whether by the use of drugs, surgery, manipulation, electricity, or any physical, mechanical, or other means whatsoever

drug_authority.value: Licensed physicians may prescribe and dispense legend drugs with board approval; may prescribe controlled substances; dispensing of legend drugs for patients' personal use outside office requires prior board approval showing need
drug_authority.quote: A physician licensed under the Arkansas Medical Practices Act ... shall not dispense legend drugs without prior approval by the Arkansas State Medical Board after application to the Arkansas State Medical Board and on the showing of need.

license_status_types.quote: The Arkansas State Medical Board may issue an academic license to practice medicine to any physician

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates must have their medical school approved by the Arkansas State Medical Board and must additionally: (1) serve 3 years as intern/resident/fellow in accredited postgraduate program in the US; OR (2) serve 3 years in postgraduate program outside US, complete all USMLE steps, obtain ECFMG certification, and complete 1+ year ACGME-accredited fellowship or receive ABMS certification; OR (3) complete 1 year in accredited postgraduate program in US and be enrolled in accredited postgraduate program in Arkansas. For temporary license in critical shortage areas, foreign graduates must have passed ECFMG examination.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: A foreign medical school whose entrance requirements and course of instruction have been approved by the Arkansas State Medical Board. (b) He or she must also have: (1) Served three (3) years as an intern, resident, or fellow, or a combination thereof, in an accredited postgraduate medical education program in the United States

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: The Arkansas State Medical Board is authorized to promulgate rules limiting the amount of Schedule II narcotics that may be prescribed and dispensed by licensees. A physician shall not be subject to disciplinary action solely for prescribing dangerous or controlled drugs for relief of chronic intractable pain when within appropriate criteria.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: Promulgate rules limiting the amount of Schedule II narcotics that may be prescribed and dispensed by licensees of the board.

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: Healthcare services provided by telemedicine, including a prescription through telemedicine, shall be held to the same standard of care as healthcare services provided in person. A professional relationship must be established before providing telemedicine services. A physician licensed in Arkansas who has access to a patient's personal health record may use telemedicine, including the telephone, with a patient located in Arkansas to diagnose, treat, and if clinically appropriate, prescribe a noncontrolled drug.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: Healthcare services provided by telemedicine, including without limitation a prescription through telemedicine, shall be held to the same standard of care as healthcare services provided in person.

telemedicine_license_available.quote: Any physician who seeks licensure in this state pursuant to the requirements of § 17-95-206, upon submission of the proper credentialing documents to the Arkansas State Medical Board, shall be issued a temporary license to practice medicine in this state until such time as final action is taken by the board on the physician's application.

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: Supervision of a graduate registered physician shall be continuous and require the physical presence of the supervising physician at the place that the services are rendered.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: A supervising physician may delegate prescriptive authority to a graduate registered physician to include prescribing, ordering, and administering Schedules III-V controlled substances, all legend drugs, and all nonschedule prescription medications and medical devices. A graduate registered physician's level of prescriptive authority shall not exceed the authority of the supervising physician.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: A physician who is supervising a graduate registered physician may delegate prescriptive authority to a graduate registered physician to include prescribing, ordering, and administering Schedules III-V controlled substances as described in the Uniform Controlled Substances Act

max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.quote: Limit supervision to no more than two (2) graduate registered physicians per supervising physician.

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: The Arkansas Medical Society, Inc. shall have the authority to establish a physicians' health committee ... to undertake the functions and responsibilities to carry out the purposes of this subchapter

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: If the Arkansas State Medical Board has reason to believe that a physician is impaired ... either board may cause an evaluation of the physician or dentist to be conducted by the appropriate committee for the purpose of determining if there is an impairment.
